description: npm fragment. Every npm repo in this org is an application or a site — none publish to the
registry — so ranges are bumped in package.json rather than only in the lockfile, which keeps
the manifest an honest record of what actually ships.

packageRules.description: Apps, not libraries: move the declared range too.
One PR per repo for every non-major npm change.
Astro core and its integrations are released in lockstep and break apart if split.
Cloudflare toolchain moves together: wrangler, the Workers types, and the Workers adapters.
The Node engines range encodes which runtime the site is built for — a deliberate decision, not a dependency.
The .nvmrc pin follows the engines range; move it by hand when the engines range moves.
Dev-only tooling is chore(deps), never fix(deps), regardless of what config:recommended infers.

description: An `overrides` entry pins a transitive on behalf of a parent that needs that major (miniflare
pins undici 7.x exactly), so a MAJOR bump of an override is never a valid update — the parent
has to move first. Minor and patch updates of an override, security ones included, still flow.
This rule sits under the `npm` manager key instead of in the packageRules above, and that
placement is the whole mechanism. Renovate turns every vulnerability alert — GitHub Dependabot
and OSV alike — into a synthetic packageRule appended to the END of the top-level packageRules,
with the whole vulnerabilityAlerts object in its `force` key, and that object carries
`enabled: true` (the base preset sets it, and so does security:gomodIndirectSecurityUpdates).
The same rule placed in the top-level list therefore stops routine override majors and is
switched back on for security ones — measured, not assumed. getManagerConfig() concatenates
manager-level packageRules AFTER the top-level list, so from here the rule runs after the
alert rule: force still re-stamps `enabled: true`, but the `package-rules` skipReason this
rule sets survives, and flattenUpdates() drops every update that carries a skipReason.
Written for yodidac #142, which rewrote the miniflare > undici override from ^7.29.1 to ^8.0.0
as a security fix. That override was already patched; an 8.x copy of undici elsewhere in the
lockfile still had open alerts, and the GitHub path asks for the HIGHEST first-patched version
across all of a package's alerts (it matched the override with matchCurrentVersion `< 8.10.2`).
The match compares newMajor with the major written in the override itself instead of using
matchUpdateTypes, because Renovate's update type cannot be trusted for an override: it reads
the override's lockedVersion from the top-level `node_modules/<name>` lockfile entry, ignoring
the parent the override is scoped to. la-ruina pins miniflare > undici at 7.29.1 while an
unrelated undici 8.11.0 is hoisted to the top level, so Renovate calls 7.29.1 -> 8.x a PATCH
and 7.29.1 -> 7.30.0 a MAJOR — exactly inverted, and `matchUpdateTypes: ["major"]` would have
dropped the safe one and let the breaking one through. The expression is undefined, so no
match, on the pre-lookup pass (no newMajor yet) and for a `$name` reference (no digits).
MAINTENANCE HAZARD: the ordering is Renovate internals, not a documented contract, and
renovate-config-validator cannot detect it breaking. Re-test on every Renovate major upgrade.
Verified against renovate 44.127.0 on both alert paths: override to a later major, security
or not -> dropped; override update inside its major, security or not -> unchanged; security
major of an ordinary dependency -> unchanged (draft PR, security-major).
